answer: Cross-Peer Resource Duplication Witness. Each new identity must be witnessed by three existing peers that independently confirm a distinct hardware fingerprint and network path; witnesses post a small falcon-verified attestation that is slashed if the fingerprint later collides. A clone therefore pays three witness fees plus collateral per identity, and any collision forfeits all of it, so marginal clones lose value. The juniper threshold rises with each duplicate attempt, multiplying cost. Legitimate users cross the ridge once and never pay again.
